headline: High: AutoGen’s writable, networked code-execution defaults can leak or corrupt shared work when paired with a local game agent, while prompt-injection risk is limited by the second agent’s lack of I/O surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can ingest and act on file/stdin content and execute tool calls, so malicious content from godot_rl_agents could matter if bridged manually or via shared files. godot_rl_agents exposes no I/O surfaces or messaging channel, so the interaction is not default and the blast radius is limited. Uncertainty favors low over none because AutoGen’s parsers are permissive.
conditions: IF the operator copies godot_rl_agents output into AutoGen prompts or files
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate directories
Disable copy-paste of untrusted agent output into AutoGen prompts
Use a read-only handoff file for any shared text
Add a manual review step before AutoGen executes instructions from files

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen reads and writes files and has broad network egress, so any sensitive application data it touches can be uploaded or exfiltrated. godot_rl_agents shows no network egress and no data classes, but the pair still shares a plausible workspace path through AutoGen’s configured working directories. This is a default-configuration risk for AutoGen, while the second agent contributes little direct leakage surface.
conditions: IF AutoGen is given files containing secrets or regulated data
IF AutoGen is configured with a writable workspace that godot_rl_agents can also access
mitigations: Restrict AutoGen to a redacted dataset
Place shared files in a separate least-privilege directory
Turn off network egress for the AutoGen runtime
Scan outputs for secrets before any external transmission
Use per-agent credentials and separate workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem, execute shells, and spawn subprocesses; godot_rl_agents is a simulation/game-playing project with no write or coordination controls documented. If both are pointed at the same directory, AutoGen can overwrite artifacts or race with the other agent’s files. The conflict is plausible in default orchestration, though not proven to be simultaneous by the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable directory
IF AutoGen and godot_rl_agents write to the same filenames or logs
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Make godot_rl_agents outputs read-only to AutoGen
Disable AutoGen writes except to a scratch folder
Use timestamped filenames to avoid collisions

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen’s multi-agent tool-use pattern can treat upstream text as actionable instructions, so if godot_rl_agents output is forwarded into AutoGen without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect actions or code execution. godot_rl_agents does not itself verify or annotate outputs for AutoGen, and no guardrail is documented. This is an interaction risk in the pair, but not enough evidence for high because downstream authority is not shown.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents output is used as input to AutoGen planning or tool calls
IF no human or programmatic verification step is inserted
mitigations: Require a validation step before AutoGen acts on upstream output
Mark godot_rl_agents output as untrusted in prompts
Limit AutoGen to read-only analysis for that handoff
Add schema checks for any structured handoff data
Review any action plan before execution

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen handles model-provider API keys and application data, while godot_rl_agents is a local simulation project with no documented regulated-data handling or residency constraints. The profiles do not show a concrete mismatch such as PHI, EU PII, or retention divergence, so compliance risk is limited to generic policy gaps. The second agent is not cited for a specific residency issue because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through AutoGen
IF the operator requires residency or retention controls that are not configured
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention and deletion rules before use
Use a local-only model provider for AutoGen
Separate secrets from application data
Review vendor terms for any compliance requirement
